text: Core concepts. doeff is built from three pieces: effects, handlers, and continuations.
An effect is a plain value that names an operation. By itself, it does nothing.
A handler receives the effect together with k, the rest of the program, and decides what the effect means.
A program is a generator. It pauses at each yield and hands the effect outward.
The innermost handler whose annotation matches the effect receives it.
Ask is not a Fetch, so typed is skipped without a call, and Ask goes on out to the reader handler.
Fetch reaches typed. Both answers come back, and greeting returns.
A handler stays installed around k. The rest of the program still runs under it.
after receives Step load, and resumes k. Inside k, Step train reaches the same handler again.
Each Resume gives back the result of the rest, and after adds to it on the way out.
What a handler does with k decides what the effect means. Here is one program under six handlers.
Resume it, and the rest runs with the answer.
Throw into it, and the program sees the error at the yield.
Pass the effect on, and the next handler out answers instead.
Hold k while other tasks run, then resume it. The scheduler works this way.
Or drop it. The rest never runs, and the handler's value is the answer.
k is one-shot. Resuming it a second time raises a RuntimeError.
Handlers compose by nesting. Each one wraps the program the next one returns.
Ask stops at reader. Get and Put pass reader and writer, and reach state.
writer answers Tell by yielding a Get and a Put of its own, which travel out to state too.
So the order matters. Put state inside writer, and writer's Get finds no handler: an unhandled effect.
Calling an at-do function runs nothing yet. It builds a program, an Expand node.
run takes that one program, evaluates it, and returns its value.
Each yield splits the program in two: the expression, and the rest, waiting for its result.
A control node, the VM evaluates itself. An effect goes to the handlers, with the rest as k.
The answer is sent back into the generator until it returns, here with Ada.
Effects name operations. Handlers decide what they mean, by what they do with k. That is the core of doeff.
